turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, and when?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A wrong quotation. Students get Shakespeare wrong all the time, Hale, and that costs marks, not the whole essay. Show me the page.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Claire won her appeal, and you just used my daughter's name to explain a zero on my son's essay. I'm writing that down, and I'll be in the principal's office before my call.
You haven't shown me the page, and the zero is still in the gradebook. Until one of those changes, I'm going upstairs.
